review.verdict: REVISION REQUIRED (narrow), lens E1, correction 5C-1. Does 5C-1 now resolve doc 49's P2? Mostly, but not fully. The structural defect is fixed in design, and the projections match the source readers. Lot quantity, version and updated_at churn is out of global invalidation, and quantity is now protected by exact lot FOR SHARE plus a fresh re-read. Allocatability and lot INSERT stay covered. Members and partners are narrowed to the columns their readers consume. Grants are OUT, and no QO reader exists for them. Binding and transfer INSERTs still advance the epoch. Shipping, media and launch-control readers are now listed. The preserved core is unchanged. One P2 remains, introduced by the correction's exact-lock alternative: the legal-binding reader also matches on alias_refs and refuses when the match is ambiguous, so whether another binding exists is a decision input. FOR SHARE cannot block a phantom INSERT of such a binding, and INSERT is now excluded. Rates and the refusal budget are honestly labelled unmeasured and reserved, but not stated. The census is not fully closed: it omits the founder checkout relation. It is also unclear whether statements that change no protected column still take the head. No reserved decision is made.

findings.claim: The exact-row-lock alternative for research_early_access_legal_bindings is unsound. The QO member-path reader's decision depends on no other binding naming the actor's handle as an alias. The correction removes INSERT protection, so a concurrent alias-bearing INSERT is a phantom that no row lock blocks.
findings.evidence: 20260809130000:290@3e82154: where customer_ref=p_customer_ref OR p_customer_ref=any(alias_refs); :295-296 raises 'ambiguous legal binding' (21000) when more than one row matches. The writer checks conflicts only by the new row's own customer_ref (:259-260); the table constrains only customer_ref<>all(alias_refs) (:31-47). Reader path: express.ts:120-128 -> directory forCustomer :208-214 -> production-deps.ts:525-526. A second binding naming C1 as an alias (an ordinary multi-handle verification) inserted after revalidation and before commit is not blocked by FOR SHARE on R1. Packet:15 itself says row locks miss phantoms; doc 49's verifier note called INSERT exclusion safe here.
findings.fix: Keep legal_bindings INSERT with cardinality(alias_refs)>0 advancing the global epoch (the table is append-only and the writer is verification-rate). Alternatively, record_legal_binding and the intake take one advisory key per handle, covering customer_ref and each alias (intake shared, before the head). Add an evidence case: an alias insert after intake revalidation refuses.

findings.claim: Excluding quantity from invalidation fixes epoch refusals, but the correction does not say whether a statement that changes no protected column still takes the head. findings.evidence: packet:11 keeps 'writer ordering independently' and :5 keeps the reserve/release/expiry replacements, whose rationale (prior proposal :29-31) assumes an AFTER-statement guard takes H on lot updates. verdicts.note: Mechanism confirmed, severity lowered from P2. The reader matches customer_ref=p OR p=any(alias_refs) and raises 21000 when more than one row matches (20260809130000:280-298@3e82154). The writer checks conflicts only by its own customer_ref (:259-260), and the table only enforces customer_ref<>all(alias_refs) (:45-48). QO reaches this reader through viewers.customer (express.ts:121-129; server/index.ts:1005-1006; production.ts:44). So FOR SHARE on R1 does not stop an alias-bearing INSERT, which contradicts packet:9/:15. Why P3: the race is serializable with the intake first, because the writer reads neither intake rows nor anything the intake writes, and the reader has no as-of time predicate. The writer has no production server constructor (SupabaseEarlyAccessLegalBindingWriter appears only at :385 and in tests). Doc 49's verifier used the same reasoning to lower F3 ('no head cycle can form'). The fix stays: keep legal-binding INSERT advancing.

Confirmed: for admin_attested bindings, forCustomer -> attestationIsPermitted -> checkoutCustomerRef reads research_early_access_cart_checkout_for_number, which selects record (supabase-legal-binding-directory.ts:221-225, :320-347; 20260807193000:174-183@3e82154). Checkouts are not among the 23 relations (packet:53-77), and packet:11 makes that a drafting blocker. Precision fix: the reader consumes only record->>'customerRef'. disposition is a writer input (hardening :249-256). The record is mutated by paymentState jsonb_set (20260808100000:618-620), so the fix should lock the founder row exactly, projected on customerRef, not as a complete row. The visibility-source gap is confirmed: visibility is required and null throws (quick-order/catalog.ts:43-44, :134-139).

Confirmed unspecified. Prior D:98 says only 'advances once per statement if its projection changes', and packet:11 and :17 never say whether the head is taken. Strengthened: under the narrowed lot projection, release (:924-930), expiry (:1378-1384) and apply_inventory_movement (coa-admin :851-859) change only quantity, version and updated_at, and reserve's other writes (:629 onward) are not among the 23 relations. If an unchanged projection takes no head, none of them takes the head. The head-inversion rationale for their replacement (prior :31-33) then disappears. What remains is ordering against the intake's lot FOR SHARE: FEFO 'for update of l' (:580-584) versus UUID order ends in a deadlock or lock-timeout refusal. Packet:5 still asserts the replacements without re-deriving why.

The relations at :26-32 are never labelled IN or OUT of the epoch; packet:19 only implies OUT. Session bindings (:28/:67) are IN for UPDATE/DELETE on an append-only table (identity migration :214-234), which is harmless but unlabelled.

Confirmed not carried: there is no writer table with a unique-index column, and the :720 and :873/:881 acquisitions are not classified (coa-admin :720@3e82154; referral V1 :873-881). Reserve's 'skip non-qualifying candidates, refuse only when insufficient' behaviour (:598-606, :623-625) is not stated. Mitigation: doc 49:121 assigned these to 'the next records delta', and this packet is scoped to the three P2s (it carries only the recipient P3, :148). Under the narrowed projection, :720 may become moot if quantity-only statements take no head (see E1-F3). bind's :879 insert still hits the PK and referral_v1_touch_binding_unique (:117, :139) after advancing.

That conforms to the standing rule (budget approval is reserved, missing evidence is NOT PROVEN), so it is not a design defect. The residual gap is that the remaining refusal sources are not listed. Doc 49:117 asked for expected rates and a budget. Packet:83 also drops prior :126's 'writer-versus-writer with H held and no intake' measurement from the future-evidence list.

verify.verdictOpinion:
The lens's verdict (REVISION REQUIRED, narrow, one P2) overstates E1-F1. The mechanism is real: an alias-bearing legal-binding INSERT is a phantom that the exact row lock does not block, which contradicts packet:9/:15. But it leaves the history serializable with the intake first, the reader has no as-of predicate, and the writer is service-role only. By doc 49's own calibration that is P3. With every finding at P3, correction 5C-1 resolves doc 49's P2 in structure. Lot quantity, version and updated_at churn is out of global invalidation, and quantity is protected by exact FOR SHARE plus a fresh re-read. Allocatability and phantoms stay covered. Members and partners are narrowed to the columns their readers consume. Grants are OUT. Binding and transfer INSERTs advance. Shipping, media and launch controls are censused. The preserved core is restated. The rate and budget sub-item becomes an honestly UNKNOWN, Samuel-reserved prerequisite: NOT PROVEN, not a design defect. Before any guard body is drafted, these P3s must be carried:
- Legal-binding INSERT advances.
- The founder checkout row is locked, projected on customerRef.
- The visibility source is stated.
- Every relation is labelled IN or OUT of the epoch.
- The design states whether unchanged projections take the head, and re-derives the writer replacements.
- Doc 49's P3 writer-table items are carried.
- The inventory predicate and lock-set size are defined.
- The design names where the referral reader's output lands in Quick Order, or puts the referral family OUT. At 3e82154 Quick Order has no referral consumer, which is the most consequential miss.
My recommended disposition is COMPATIBLE AS DESIGN for 5C-1 with these P3 carry-forwards. A reviewer who applies doc 49's literal rule ('keep INSERT advancing where absence is a decision input') may keep F1 at P2, which needs a one-line fix. Either way, compatibility grants no source, installation or execution authority. No reserved decision is made: Health legal pair, offer/quantity/destination, commission attribution, budget, writer scope and GATE-01 all stay with Samuel.

review.verdict: COMPATIBLE AS DESIGN for lens E2 (5C-2 and 5C-3 only). Both doc 49 P2s are resolved. 5C-2 now requires the same role OID for the sessions owner, nonce owner, provider-fence owner and the commit owner (the role that takes the locks), with rolsuper or rolbypassrls. It also requires effective privileges on every touched relation, including UPDATE for FOR SHARE. Precheck, reapply, postcheck and runtime checks must refuse when the precondition fails or drifts. No grant, role or RLS change may be used to repair it, the sessions prefix is not used, and hosted ownership is stated as NOT PROVEN. 5C-3 now has a schemaVersion literal and a closed key list with types, bounds and nullability. It defines the canonical bytes exactly (display key order, no whitespace/BOM/newline, NFC, escaping, integers, byte-order sorting, re-encode equality, never jsonb::text). The digest rule is: exactly one normalized_decision_inputs artifact whose digest is the SHA-256 of the stored text, with no circular bundleSha256. Samuel's values fill the keys, and the browser chooses nothing. No P0, P1 or P2 remains. Eleven P3s should go into the next delta before the validator or installer is drafted. Two doc 49 P3s: the recipient P3 is addressed; the budget-consequence P3 is not. Missing: commit and helper names that keep the new function out of the existing fingerprint namespaces, the validator object, uniqueness of artifact kinds, a few undecidable validator rules, and the census bytes. This lens grants no source, installation or execution authority and makes none of the reserved decisions.

verdicts.note: Upheld. Packet :87 names only the sessions, nonce, fence and commit owners. currentness.sql:171-173@3e82154 raises unless current_user = relowner(authority_head). Its table-ACL drift check (:190-196) refuses any grantee other than the owner on authority_% tables. So a grant cannot be the fix, and a superuser that is not the owner still fails :171. Intakes forces RLS (intake.sql:135), and the verifier allows an owner-only ACL (:406-412). Both owners equal the fence owner only at install time: intake :343-345 and :402, currentness :353-355@f581b6b. Drift after install is possible. The fix is correct.

Upheld. Packet :91 says only 'Prefer qualified objects/search_path=pg_catalog'. verify.verdictOpinion:
I uphold the lens verdict: compatible as design for 5C-2 and 5C-3. Both doc 49 P2s are resolved at the level of their smallest corrections. I find no P0, P1 or P2. All eleven lens findings stand at P3, and the anchors match the Git objects at 3e82154 and f581b6b. The packet copies match their blobs at 462cf79 and f1821b6.

Corrections to the lens:
- Canonical encoding moves from PASS to PARTIAL: the set arrays and 'controls' are undefined.
- 'Values fill keys, not shape' moves from PASS to PARTIAL, because of the single Health agreement and the shipping-state destination form.
- Validator placement moves from FAIL to PARTIAL: prior :68 still applies.
- E2-3 must also name the intake precheck and postcheck :131, and must flag that amending the intake family needs owner scope.

Six further P3s were missed, listed under missed. The next delta must carry all of them before any validator, precheck or commit body is drafted.

Standing rules hold. This compatible design grants no source, installation or execution authority. The reserved decisions stay with Samuel and are not made here: Health pair content and cardinality, offer, quantity, audience and destination policy, revocation ordering and budget, and writer-side lock policy. Hosted ownership, bypass rights, encoding and NFC support remain NOT PROVEN. Nothing was executed.
